releaseClaim.userOperation: An operator changes the system default model live and a person chatting sees the next eligible reply answered by the model they expect — following the new default, keeping a conversation override, inheriting after clearing it — with a receipt naming the model that actually answered, its origin and when the change took effect; an in-flight reply finishes on its model.
supportedEnvironments: web console in the local browser against UAR with embedded SurrealDB 4.0.0 (server-full), synthetic stub providers
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: On the current tree (identical to f2c9e36e for src, frontend/src and catalog) the live default route POST /api/uar/providers/{id}/default persists llm.default_provider and swaps the registry default, but checks only that the provider exists, so a disabled provider is accepted. The console offers a per-provider "Set as default" button and no system default picker. The settings API still accepts writes to llm.default_provider. A saved session model controls inference (prior REST receipt B36 on an earlier build proves default and override routing and restart survival); the Session Configuration sheet clears an override by setting an empty value with no preview, and no transcript receipt shows the serving model, its origin or when a change took effect. PolicyScope has no system-default origin. Catalog Model identity is provider-qualified on the REST path. The stub CLI has no delayed reply kind.

functionalScope: S1-R1 Live default: an authorized operator changes the system default A to B through the dedicated live route; confirmation shows only after the runtime acknowledges; no restart

S1-R2 Next eligible turn: a conversation with no override answers its next turn on B, and the transcript shows the model that actually answered, its origin (system default) and when the change took effect
S1-R3 Override holds: a conversation with override C keeps answering on C after the default change, shown with origin "this conversation"
S1-R4 Clear to inherit: clearing the override previews the inherited value B before confirming, and the next turn answers on B
S1-R5 Isolation: changing or clearing one conversation's override does not change another conversation
S1-R6 In-flight binding: a turn already generating when the default changes finishes on the model it started with
S1-R7 Truthful failure: an unavailable or disabled choice is refused with a usable reason, the previous effective value stays and is shown, and nothing reports the requested model as served
S1-R8 Agent pin: an agent with an explicit model keeps it and is listed as pinned when the default changes
S1-R9 Served model, not requested model: the receipt names the model id the provider reported as serving and never shows the requested candidate as the answering model
Supporting dependency (SCN-SET-003): the settings API rejects writes to llm.default_provider, so the live route is the only system-default writer
Supporting dependency (SCN-IDN-001): one provider-qualified Model identity holds under shared bare model ids
Supporting dependency (SCN-PICK-002): the model picker the operator and chat user drive is searchable and keyboard operable

requiredSafetyChecks.description: Test scripts never require, mint, renew or send authentication credentials (JWTs, bearer tokens, login credentials, admin keys). Provider API keys for scratch stub providers are fixture data and allowed (the BDD config sets UAR_LLM__API_KEY=test-stub-key). Enforced by the independent runner and step-definition review. BDD runs use the deployment auth-off test configuration (tests/bdd/playwright.config.ts sets UAR_SECURITY__JWT_REQUIRED=false and UAR_SECURITY__SETTINGS_MUTATION_AUTH_REQUIRED=false) and send no credentials; supporting runs send none either.
The settings API cannot write llm.default_provider; the live default route is the only system-default writer and a direct settings write leaves the live default and stored row unchanged.
A refused or unavailable model choice is never reported as served: no receipt names it and no request reaches the stub for it.

evidenceInvalidation: Every invalidationKeys entry is a repository path or git pathspec glob. After an authorized repair, a scenario's or negative control's earlier evidence carries forward to the repaired candidate only when `git diff --name-only <old candidateCommit> <new candidateCommit>` lists no path matching any of its keys; otherwise it is invalidated and reruns on the new candidate. Every S1 scenario shares one key set covering the console source (frontend/src/**, frontend/packages/**), the server source (src/**, vendor/**), the files compiled into the server (migrations/** embedded through include_str! and sqlx::migrate!, build.rs, proto/**, data/model_benchmarks.json, docs/agents/**), rust-toolchain.toml, build manifests and lockfiles, catalog/** and tests/bdd/**, because each one drives the whole application through the browser; supporting scenarios also key on frontend/e2e/** and their Playwright configs. Both mutant controls always rerun after a repair, because their worktrees are recreated from the new candidate. A change to this contract, s1-oracle.json, either feature file, baseline-verdicts.json or boundary-baseline-expectations.json is an amendment under amendmentPolicy, never a repair. History is preserved.
